findings.reason: E2B issue #1900 and Daytona issue #3859 exist and report MCP gateway/tool-listing problems, but the available evidence does not substantiate broad recurring demand or meaningful engagement; #3859 itself says the reporter is unsure whether the issue is real.

The E2B, microsandbox, and Anthropic sandbox-runtime issues exist and request credential or secret handling that avoids plaintext exposure. The evidence supports recurring interest, but not the claimed common proxy-layer implementation or engagement level.

Coder #6815 exists, is open, and explicitly requests syncing work locally for offline use and back to a Coder workspace. The claimed reaction count and “top-reaction” ranking were not verifiable from the opened page; one issue alone does not support strong status.

The cited Claude Code, Codex, and DeepAgents issues are real and request more permissive or granular tool approval. However, the Claude and Codex issues are closed, DeepAgents is labeled backlog, and engagement counts were unavailable; strong status is unsupported.

Microsandbox #47 exists, but requests native Windows host support without WSL, not a Windows guest OS. The claimed additional E2B and Daytona evidence was not captured, so cross-repo demand for Windows guests is unconfirmed.

The primary Agent Browser issue could not be opened successfully. The listed standalone repositories demonstrate supply/ecosystem activity, not verified user demand, and no cited sandbox-repository issue confirms the stated cross-repo theme.

Daytona #4232 exists and documents a broken self-hosted Kubernetes/containerd deployment. It is an operational bug report rather than a feature request; the E2B issue and both stated reaction counts could not be confirmed, so moderate recurring demand is unsupported.

Both cited Daytona issues exist and are open feature requests, but #2909 requests CLI profiles for multiple Daytona installations, while #3309 requests local-to-sandbox live file synchronization. Neither establishes demand for predictable or reusable sandbox resource management. The claimed three reactions on each could not be confirmed because GitHub did not expose reactions in the opened pages; #3309 also has no comments or assignee.
